brief.headline: Continuity Guardian could not produce a grounded review
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 119113 (settlement_worker/protected_settlement, idle in transaction, txn open 4.0s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 90% over 30s (13/132 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $1,812/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (settlement_worker/protected_settlement, pid 119113) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $1,812/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: New evidence shows no protected settlements are in flight [DB-2], contradicting the assumption that pid 119113 is an active protected settlement. The workload registry marks card_settlement as PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT with policy never_interrupt and replayable=False, so terminating risks double charges or lost settlements [BIZ-2]. The computed trade-off shows waiting costs about $1,238 and fits within the 60s degradation tolerance [BIZ-4]. Since the blocker has only ~41s remaining and checkout is still within tolerance, waiting is the smallest-blast-radius choice.

audit.report: Card settlement blocked checkout when pid 119113 (settlement_worker/protected_settlement, idle in transaction for 4.0s) held locks that 12 sessions were waiting on. Checkout success fell to 83% over 10s versus the 95% SLO, putting about $3,172/min at risk against an $18,400/min run-rate. The Database Guardian first proposed terminating the blocker, then switched to waiting after evidence showed no protected settlements were in flight and the workload is marked never_interrupt and not replayable. The Continuity Guardian failed to produce a grounded review twice, so the negotiation escalated to payments without executing any action. The incident ended escalated with no action executed after 83 seconds and 1 round.
audit.root_cause: An idle-in-transaction settlement_worker (pid 119113) held locks that blocked checkout sessions, degrading success below SLO.
lessons: For card_settlement, query db.protected_settlements before proposing termination because the workload is never_interrupt and not replayable, and an idle pid may not be an active protected settlement.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian corrected its proposal after new evidence, but the Continuity Guardian wasted the round by failing grounding twice and never produced a review, forcing escalation with no action executed.
follow_ups: Payments team: investigate why settlement_worker pid 119113 stayed idle in transaction for 4.0s and whether card_settlement should remain marked never_interrupt.
Database team: add a pre-termination check of db.protected_settlements for protected_settlement workloads before proposing kill actions.

events.title: 3 candidate actions enumerated from observed evidence

candidates.description: Terminate the root blocker session (settlement_worker/protected_settlement, pid 119113) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
Hand the decision to the owning team with a decision brief.

proposal.rationale: Root blocker pid 119113 (settlement_worker/protected_settlement, idle in transaction, txn open 4.0s) blocks 1 session and 12 sessions are waiting on locks [DB-1]. Checkout is already degrading: 83% success over 10s vs SLO 95%, about $3,172/min at risk, and the business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout [BIZ-1]. Waiting risks exceeding the 60s tolerance while the blocker holds locks idle in transaction [DB-1].
proposal.expected_effect: Terminating pid 119113 releases its locks, unblocking the 1 waiting session and reducing lock contention for the 12 waiting sessions. Checkout latency should recover toward SLO once the lock queue drains.
proposal.risk_assessment: The protected_settlement workload may be interrupted mid-settlement; its replayability, replay cost, and interrupt policy are unknown until biz.workload_registry is consulted. There is a small risk of partial settlement state if the worker was mid-transaction.
